p: householder: God is bound to no man, and therefore he calls whoever and whenever he desires. This only every man ought to take heed of, and upon this bestow his whole endeavour, that he go forward and come to the mark without stopping at all or staggering, and to not curiously examine the doings of other men, or the judgments of God.
agreed with the labourers for a: Literally, "fell in time": it is a kind of speech taken from poetry.
eleventh hour he went out: The last hour: for the day was twelve hours long, and the first hour began at sunrise.

evil: Naught, that is to say, do you envy at my goodness towards them? For by an "evil eye" the Hebrews mean "envy", because such dispositions appear chiefly in the eyes, as above in Mt 6:23. It is set in opposition to the word "single", and it is taken there for corrupt: for whereas he said before in verse 22, "If thine eye be single", he adds in verse 23, "but if thine eye by wicked", or "corrupt", the word being the same in that place as it is here. Mt 6:22,23
And Jesus going up to Jerusalem: Christ goes to the cross necessarily, and yet willingly.
Behold: They that should be persecuting him the least, are the greatest persecutors of Christ.
And shall deliver him to the: The shame of the cross is the sure way to the glory of everlasting life.
Then came to him the mother: The manner of the heavenly kingdom is quite contrary to the earthly kingdom.

drink of the cup that I: "Taking the cup" is figurative speech for that which is contained in the cup. And again, the Hebrews understand by the word "cup", sometimes the manner of punishment which is rendered to sin, as Ps 11:6, or the joy that is given to the faithful, as Ps 23:5, and sometimes a lot or condition, as Ps 16:5.
baptism that I am baptized with: This is in reference to afflictions, as David commonly uses.
not mine to give: The almightiness of Christ's divinity is not shut out by this, but it shows the debasing of himself by taking man's nature upon him.
dominion over them: Somewhat sharply and roughly.
And as they departed from Jericho: Christ by healing these blind men with only one touch, shows that he is the only light of the world.
called them: Himself, not by the means of other men.
